newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary launches "NATOpoly" boardgame for Madrid.
newsitem.headline: Hungary launches "NATOpoly" boardgame for Madrid.

text.p: A computer game launched on Friday will let ordinary Hungarians haggle with NATO's Secretary General over the costs of the country's accession into the Alliance.

Hungary, which is expected to be invited to NATO along with the Czech Republic and Poland at the alliance's Madrid summit next week, has launched the game as part of the government's domestic pro-NATO campaign ahead of a referendum next year.
"We have to dispel decades-old misconceptions about NATO," Hungarian Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs told a news conference.
The game, NATOpoly, also allows the player to re-enact historic decisions since World War II, acting as Charles de Gaulle or Winston Churchill.
In the game, a series of wrong decisions and a spell of bad luck could result in the player being refused NATO entry.
Kovacs, however, is confident that Hungary has all the right answers to pass the real-life test.
"I hope that in the spring of 1999 we can celebrate NATO's fiftieth anniversary as full members," he said.
